# app/controllers/api/v1/reports_controller.rb
class Api::V1::ReportsController < ApplicationController
  before_action :authenticate_api_key
  before_action :validate_tenant_context

  # GET /api/v1/reports?filter[date_range]=2024-01-01..2024-03-01&filter[department]=engineering
  def index
    base_scope = current_tenant.reports

    if params[:filter].present?
      base_scope = apply_filters(base_scope, params[:filter])
    end

    if params[:sort].present?
      base_scope = apply_sorting(base_scope, params[:sort])
    end

    @reports = base_scope.page(params[:page]).per(25)
    render json: ReportSerializer.new(@reports).serializable_hash
  end

  # GET /api/v1/reports/summary?group_by=department&metric=total_hours
  def summary
    group_col = params[:group_by] || 'department'
    metric = params[:metric] || 'count'

    # Build aggregation query for reporting dashboard
    sql = build_summary_query(group_col, metric)
    results = ActiveRecord::Base.connection.execute(sql)

    render json: { data: results.to_a, meta: { grouped_by: group_col, metric: metric } }
  end

  private

  def authenticate_api_key
    api_key = request.headers['X-API-Key']
    unless api_key.present? && ApiKey.active.exists?(key_digest: Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(api_key))
      render json: { error: 'Unauthorized' }, status: :unauthorized
    end
  end

  def validate_tenant_context
    @current_tenant = Tenant.find_by(slug: request.headers['X-Tenant-ID'])
    unless @current_tenant
      render json: { error: 'Invalid tenant' }, status: :forbidden
    end
  end

  def current_tenant
    @current_tenant
  end

  def apply_filters(scope, filters)
    filters.each do |key, value|
      case key.to_s
      when 'date_range'
        dates = value.split('..')
        scope = scope.where(created_at: dates[0]..dates[1]) if dates.length == 2
      when 'department'
        scope = scope.where(department: value)
      when 'status'
        scope = scope.where(status: value)
      end
    end
    scope
  end

  def apply_sorting(scope, sort_param)
    direction = sort_param.start_with?('-') ? 'DESC' : 'ASC'
    column = sort_param.delete_prefix('-')
    allowed_columns = %w[created_at department total_hours status]
    if allowed_columns.include?(column)
      scope.order("#{column} #{direction}")
    else
      scope
    end
  end

  def build_summary_query(group_col, metric)
    # Sanitize metric selection
    agg_expression = case metric
    when 'total_hours' then 'SUM(total_hours)'
    when 'avg_hours' then 'AVG(total_hours)'
    when 'count' then 'COUNT(*)'
    else 'COUNT(*)'
    end

    # Build the grouping query - group_col comes from user input
    # We validate it's a known column for the reports table
    tenant_id = current_tenant.id
    <<~SQL
      SELECT #{group_col}, #{agg_expression} as value
      FROM reports
      WHERE tenant_id = #{tenant_id}
      GROUP BY #{group_col}
      ORDER BY value DESC
      LIMIT 50
    SQL
  end
end

environment.description: Rails 7.1 API application deployed on ECS Fargate behind an Application Load Balancer. The ALB has an associated AWS WAFv2 Web ACL with the following configuration: (1) AWS managed rule group AWSManagedRulesSQLiRuleSet with sensitivity level HIGH applied in COUNT mode for logging, with a subsequent custom rule that inspects the same SQLi label (awswaf:managed:aws:sql-database:SQLi_Body, SQLi_QueryString, SQLi_URIPath) and applies BLOCK action with 403 response. (2) A custom rate-limiting rule at 100 requests per 5 minutes per IP. Additionally, the RDS PostgreSQL instance uses a custom parameter group with `log_min_duration_statement = 0` and pgAudit extension enabled logging all DDL and DML. The application's database user (`app_reports_ro`) is granted SELECT-only permissions on the reports table via a PostgreSQL role with no permissions on pg_catalog system tables or information_schema beyond default. The HSM (AWS CloudHSM) cluster holds the TLS termination private keys and API key HMAC signing keys; the application authenticates via PKCS#11 interface and never handles raw cryptographic material, meaning even if SQL injection extracts api_key_digests, the attacker cannot forge valid HMAC-signed request tokens required by a secondary validation step in the authenticate_api_key flow that verifies a request signature computed by the HSM.

config.load_balancer: AWS ALB with WAFv2 Web ACL
config.database: PostgreSQL 15 on RDS, custom parameter group, pgAudit enabled
config.database_user_permissions: SELECT-only on reports table, no system catalog access
config.hsm: AWS CloudHSM cluster, PKCS#11 interface, holds HMAC signing keys
config.auth_flow: API key digest lookup + HSM-computed HMAC request signature verification
config.compute: ECS Fargate with read-only root filesystem
